chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, concerning His saying:
Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “And whoever kills a believer intentionally”
He عليه السلام said: “Whoever kills a believer on account of his religion, then that is the intentional killer about whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has spoken in His Book.”
“And He has prepared for him a tremendous punishment.”

I said: Then a matter occurs between a man and another man, and he strikes him with his sword and kills him. He عليه السلام said: “That is not the intentional one meant by Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

key_terms.بِسَيْفِهِ: with his sword; indicating the act of striking in a dispute
key_terms.عَذَابًا عَظِيمًا: a tremendous punishment prepared for such a killer
key_terms.عَلَى دِينِهِ: on account of his religion; because of his faith
key_terms.فِي كِتَابِهِ: in His Book; meaning in the Quran
key_terms.مُؤْمِنًا: a believer; the person whose killing is under discussion
key_terms.مُتَعَمِّدًا: intentionally; here explained in a specific qualified sense

ai.seo_question: What does «وَمَنْ يَقْتُلْ مُؤْمِنًا مُتَعَمِّدًا» mean in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Quranic phrase about killing a believer intentionally as referring specifically to killing a believer because of his religion. It distinguishes that grave form of deliberate religiously motivated murder from a killing that happens during a dispute between two men. The narration thus clarifies the verse’s severe warning and its intended scope.
